name: Meursault

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

terms: France's protected place names. A wine sold under one must follow that appellation's rules. The EU's term for the same tier is PDO, or AOP in French.
Indication Géographique Protégée, the tier below AOC. It replaced vin de pays in 2009.
France's simplest category, in use since 2010. It replaced vin de table.
There is no legal or agreed definition of old, so the words promise nothing on their own.
Bourgogne, village, Premier Cru, Grand Cru
Burgundy's four levels, from regional Bourgogne up through village wines to Premier Cru and Grand Cru vineyards. The Grand Crus usually sit mid-slope and higher, with the best sun and drainage.
keyfacts: Meursault is a Côte de Beaune commune in Burgundy, and white wine from Chardonnay makes up around 98% of production.
There are no Grand Cru vineyards within Meursault, but there are several Premier Cru vineyards.
White Meursault often shows toasted almond and hazelnut notes, with butter, honey and citrus.

notes: White Meursault usually shows clear oak and malolactic fermentation, which is why it is often called buttery.
Oak brings vanilla, coconut and dill, and malolactic gives a rounder, creamier feel.
Meursault is among the roundest white Burgundies, and it turns nutty with age.

blurb.text: A Côte de Beaune appellation, about 98% white from Chardonnay, with a little red from Pinot Noir. It has no Grand Cru vineyards but several highly regarded Premier Cru vineyards.
